name: PA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+17 partisan lean anchors the race firmly in Republican territory
Reschenthaler's roughly twelve-to-one fundraising edge ($5.0M vs $406K raised)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4%
No polls or expert ratings show any sign of competitiveness
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean, Reschenthaler's dominant fundraising position, and prediction markets pricing his win odds near 95% all point to a comfortable incumbent victory, with only the favorable Democratic national environment pulling the expected margin back from the low twenties into the high teens.
model.watch: A large outside-spending surge against Reschenthaler or a sharp national shift toward Democrats could narrow the margin, though neither appears likely to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwestern Pennsylvania's 14th District leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Guy Reschenthaler is seeking re-election with a substantial financial edge. He has raised about $5.0 million and held $713,000 in cash, while Democrat Alan Bradstock has raised roughly $406,000 with $73,000 on hand. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Bradstock only about a 4% chance of winning.

The district's R+17 partisan lean anchors the forecast, softened somewhat by a national environment favoring Democrats and by the incumbent's spending advantage. Even with those adjustments, the expected margin remains in the high teens for Reschenthaler. Barring an unexpected scandal, a major outside-spending intervention, or a dramatic shift in the national climate, he is positioned to win re-election comfortably.
